- `partial_effect(undecided)`: every other `partial_effect`, that is,
  one whose admitted evidence does not establish non-attainment. The
  admitted evidence cannot decide whether the intended outcome is or will be met:
  the bounded post-observation that the
  [effect law](#mutable-subject-effect-relation) requires is not yet
  acquired, or it shows part reached while a later completion of the
  effect could still meet the outcome, or it shows the outcome met while
  the effect may still be acting, so whether the outcome is met once the
  effect settles is undecided, or a response was lost and no
  counterexample is observed. A lost response, an absent record or an
  actor's context holding no trace of the effect is no evidence about the
  subject, so it establishes neither non-attainment nor the end of the
  effect ([ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects)).

Neither core value to which the `partial` and `partial_effect` values map
records that the subject changed or whether the effect has ended. The
`partial_effect` residual and its re-entry carry both facts and survive
every join
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
Falsified never licenses treating the effect as absent; indeterminate
never licenses treating it as absent or as complete; neither licenses
treating it as ended where the evidence does not establish its end. Under
either value the explicit re-entry precedes any further effect, and an
effect whose end is not established is reconciled under
[ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart) before any
repetition (P5, P4b).

Mapping of the dispositions to the core, new in this corpus. Purpose:
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) places the results of
effects in the core. Material relation: whether an occurrence's effect
may be repeated or relied on, which is the material relation of
[ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) (P5, P6). An occurrence
intends an effect when an `EffectInvocation` names it. For such an
occurrence the disposition refines ACTIVATION §3 Effects and maps for its
predicate, "the intended effect occurred"; the causes of the two
`partial_effect` values are those stated under
[Closed constraint, judgment, residual and stop kinds](#closed-constraint-judgment-residual-and-stop-kinds):

| Disposition | Effects value | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|---|
| `completed_effect` | `completed` | satisfied | the bounded post-observation and sufficient effect evidence establish that the intended effect occurred and that the effect has ended |
| `partial_effect(not_attained)` | `not_effected` | falsified | the admitted evidence establishes that the intended outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it; the part that did occur is named with the value, and an end of the effect that the evidence does not establish is recorded beside it, not in it |
| `partial_effect(undecided)` | `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | the evidence cannot decide whether the intended outcome is or will be reached |
| `refused_effect` | `not_effected` | falsified | the evidence shows that no authorised mutation began |
| `no_effect` | `not_effected` | falsified | the admitted disposition records that no invocation was dispatched, and the record is exact because `invokes_effect` exists if and only if one was; so the occurrence effected nothing on the subject |

An occurrence that no `EffectInvocation` names intends no effect.
ACTIVATION §3 Effects poses no predicate for it, and its `no_effect`
records only that no domain effect was attempted: it is a record, not an
effect result (P5, P6).

`j_ready` judges the unchanged `EffectSubject` immediately before effect
dispatch under the application's declared currentness and invalidation
law. If the pre-observation or the grant has become stale, the effect does
not start; the application re-observes and issues a new readiness subject
and judgment, or stops. If an effect has begun and cannot establish a
complete disposition, `partial_effect` stays explicit and a bounded
post-effect observation is required. This law requires no lock or
transaction implementation (P5, P6).

Where none of these values applies, the evaluation returns a core value
directly under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results):
`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot decide its predicate,
naming the evidence that would decide; `out_of_frame` where its claim
needs a relation or capability that its frame does not declare; and
`invalid_basis` where its subject or basis cannot support it on a ground
other than `representation_space_invalid` (P5).

A verification not run. Where no ground of `extraction_inadmissible` or
`representation_space_invalid` holds, a candidate direction whose
verification has not been run has no result for direction acceptance:
the verification is the evaluation of that predicate, and it was not
performed, so it has no
closed result and is never mapped to
`indeterminate` or to any other core value
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed). The
direction stays a candidate (§10 Verification by treatment). In every
conjunction over its acceptance, the unrun verification is a planned
assessment without a closed result
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Gaps) where the verification was planned; where none was planned, the
obligation it would have discharged is uncovered coverage. A step whose output needed that verification and that stopped
without it ends `incomplete`, which
[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
maps for the predicate "a candidate is available", never to
`indeterminate`; the step's work state carries the unrun verification as
a residual ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)).
Publishing the unverified direction is `published_unverified` (P5, P6).

Mapping of the closure decision to the core result algebra, new in this
corpus. Purpose: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) states
every outcome in the core or in a refinement that maps each refined value
to exactly one core value and adds no core value. Material relation: a
composite over the edge joins each closure decision as one core value, so
a failure, an undecided closure and a needed re-entry stay distinct (P5,
P6). The closure decision is `evaluate_action`'s result over admitted
evidence, mapped for the predicate "the edge's obligations are fulfilled
on the exact basis". The bounded action it judges has its own step result
under [ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
for "a candidate is available", and neither value counts toward the
other's predicate
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
Each decision keeps its own vocabulary and its basis and reason refs
beside its core value (P5, P6).

| Decision | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `close` | satisfied | the ledger's admitted evidence fulfils the edge's obligations on the exact basis |
| `yield` | indeterminate | the edge stays lawful and the admitted evidence, progress or a waiting state, does not yet decide its obligations; the replay-visible resume basis names what would decide; no failure is classified, as A9 requires |
| `retry(defeated)` | falsified | the evidence that defeats the edge for this attempt is the counterexample; A9 separates this failure-classified re-attempt from yield |
| `retry(undecided)` | indeterminate | the attempt ended without evidence that decides the edge's obligations; the decision's reason refs name the re-attempt that would decide |
| `repair(implementation)` | falsified | the failing obligation row is the counterexample (P5, P6) |
| `repair(proof)` | indeterminate | the defect is in the proof, so the admitted evidence cannot decide the obligation; the decision's reason refs name the repaired proof that would decide (P5, P6) |
| `re-enter(undeclared)` | out_of_frame | the edge cannot close on its current basis because an upstream asset or governing relation must change, and the change needs a relation, capability or authority that no admitted basis declares; the decision names it and its owner |
| `re-enter(basis)` | invalid_basis | the edge cannot close on its current basis because an upstream asset or governing relation must change, and that basis cannot support the edge |
| `reprice` | out_of_frame | further work needs a selected outcome or bound that no admitted basis declares; the decision names it, its owner and the constitutional re-entry it requests, which is the reconfiguration pressure of out_of_frame ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or indeterminate) |
| `block(undeclared)` | out_of_frame | `evaluate_action` decides that the action just taken leaves the edge unable to proceed, because it needs a relation, capability or authority that no admitted basis declares |
| `block(basis)` | invalid_basis | `evaluate_action` decides that the action just taken leaves the edge unable to proceed on its current basis, which cannot support it |

Closure decisions and dispositions. The closure decisions of A8 and their
refined values are this member's, and they answer the edge predicate
above. The dispositions `accept`, `local_repair`, `re_enter` and `reject`
are owned by [ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition) and
answer another predicate, "the candidate is accepted at its declared
boundary". A closure decision is not a disposition and is never recorded
as one, and no disposition is a closure decision: `repair` is not
`local_repair`, and `re-enter` is not `re_enter`. Edge closure is
evidence toward acceptance and never acceptance itself (the
selected-outcome paragraphs above). Their core values differ because their
predicates differ. `repair(proof)` is `indeterminate`, because a
defective proof leaves the edge's obligations undecided, while
`local_repair` is `falsified`, because the local defect defeats
acceptance of the candidate. `re-enter(undeclared)` is `out_of_frame`,
because the change needs a relation, capability or authority that no
admitted basis declares, while `re_enter` is `invalid_basis`. Neither
value counts toward the other's predicate
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
